key_insight: Pangram 4 is a stronger AI-text detector that improves both accuracy and resilience, especially on out-of-distribution content and adversarially edited text. It achieves very high discrimination performance while keeping false positives extremely low.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of reliably detecting AI-generated text in real-world settings, including mixed AI-human writing, fine-grained edits, and adversarial attempts to evade detection.
method: Develops Pangram 4, the latest deep-learning-based AI-text classification model from Pangram Labs.
Evaluates performance using standard detection metrics such as AUROC, false positive rate, and false negative rate.
Tests robustness on out-of-distribution examples and adversarially modified text to assess real-world reliability.
impact: This matters for practitioners building content moderation, provenance, plagiarism, and AI-safety tools because it offers a more accurate and robust detector. Lower false positives and better robustness make deployment more trustworthy in production environments.
visual_elements: Performance dashboard showing AUROC, false positive rate, and false negative rate
Before-and-after comparison chart between Pangram 3 and Pangram 4
Robustness diagram illustrating in-distribution vs out-of-distribution and adversarial text
Mixed-text example panel highlighting AI-human co-authored and lightly edited passages
paper_authors: Ben Glickenhaus, Katherine Thai, Jenna Russell, Elyas Masrour, Yue Han
